title: Product of the Others
statement:
Given `nums`, build a new list `result` where `result[i]` is the **product of all the numbers in `nums` except `nums[i]`**.

Return `result`. Try to do it without dividing (the list can contain zeros).

examples.explanation: The zero makes every product 0 except the one that skips it: (-1) * 1 * (-3) * 3 = 9.

hints.nudge: result[i] is the product of everything to the left of i times the product of everything to the right of i.
hints.pseudocode:
left = 1
for i from 0 to n-1: result[i] = left; left *= nums[i]
right = 1
for i from n-1 down to 0: result[i] *= right; right *= nums[i]
hints.walkthrough: Multiplying all the others for every index costs O(n^2). Instead, make one pass from the left storing in result[i] the product of everything before i. Then make a pass from the right, multiplying result[i] by the product of everything after i. No division is needed, so zeros are handled automatically. O(n) time.
